title: Answer: the objective world consists entirely of conscious agents, though tables and chairs are not conscious

statements.text: Conscious realism holds that the objective world, the world whose existence does not depend on a particular observer's perceptions, consists entirely of conscious agents. This is not panpsychism: tables and chairs are icons in the interfaces of conscious agents, and so conscious experiences of those agents, but they are not themselves conscious. Seeing a table is interacting with a system of conscious agents through a simplified icon, while seeing another person conveys that one is interacting with a conscious agent. A rock carries much less information about the agents behind it than a face does.
statements.scope: Conscious realism and the mind-body problem (2008)

sources.quote: Conscious realism asserts that the objective world, i.e., the world whose existence does not depend on the perceptions of a particular observer, consists entirely of conscious agents.
Conscious realism is not panpsychism nor does it entail panpsychism.
It does not claim, nor entail, that tables and chairs are conscious or conscious agents.
When we look at a rock, rather than a face, we get much less information about the conscious agents
